title: Working memory
intro: The model has no other memory. It only sees the messages you send on this call. That list is working memory, and it grows with every tool result you append.

steps.author: system
steps.label: System
steps.text: You are a coding agent. Tools: read_file, edit_file, run_command.
steps.narration: Working memory starts as this messages list. The system message is about 3,100 tokens. The next call will send it again.

steps.author: user
steps.label: User
steps.text: Refactor the parser and make the tests pass.
steps.narration: The user message is the second item. print(len(messages)) reports 2. That is the whole list so far.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.narration: Your program appends the file contents as a tool result. The list is now 3. The next call sends the whole list, including this file.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.narration: Test output is appended too. The list is now 4. The model can use it only while it remains in the list.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.narration: Reading the file again appends a second copy. Your program decides what stays. The model cannot drop messages on its own.

steps.author: tool
steps.label: Tool result
steps.text: Additional file contents and test output
steps.narration: print(len(messages)) is now 6. estimate_tokens reads 168,112. Each model has a context window: a hard limit on how many tokens it can read.

steps.author: system
steps.label: Summary
steps.text: Summary: refactoring parser.py. 11 of 14 tests pass. Remaining: CSV quoting, trailing newline, Unicode escape.
steps.narration: The estimate is over TOKEN_LIMIT. summarize_if_needed keeps the system prompt and original task, and replaces the rest with one summary. That shorter list is now working memory.
